summary: None of the step-by-step methods here applies to this equation. The graph uses a numerical solution.

methods.name: Separation of variables
methods.reason: The right-hand side \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) cannot be written as a product \(g(x)\,h(y)\), so the variables cannot be separated.

methods.name: Integrating factor (linear)
methods.reason: The equation is not linear: \(y\) appears in a way other than a plain first power (for example squared, inside a function, or multiplying itself), so it cannot be written as \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\).

methods.name: Exact equation
methods.reason: Written as \(M\,dx + N\,dy = 0\), exactness needs \(\partial M/\partial y = \partial N/\partial x\). Here they are \(- 2 y\) and \(0\), and no integrating factor in one variable fixes it.

methods.name: Bernoulli substitution
methods.reason: The equation does not have the form \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\,y^n\) with \(n \ne 0, 1\).

methods.name: Homogeneous substitution (y = vx)
methods.reason: The right-hand side cannot be written as a function of \(y/x\) alone.

methods.name: Laplace transform
methods.reason: The method needs a linear equation.
